requirements.title: One process-launch gate, shared by every ACP session, spaced 1.5 seconds
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:7-21 - `private actor ACPLaunchGate` with `spacing: TimeInterval`, `nextSlot = Date.distantPast`, and `wait()`: `let now = Date.now; let slot = max(now, nextSlot); nextSlot = slot.addingTimeInterval(spacing); if slot > now { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(slot.timeIntervalSince(now))) }`
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:26 - `private static let launchGate = ACPLaunchGate(spacing: 1.5)`
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:110 - `await Self.launchGate.wait()` in start()
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:3-6 - rationale: an agent keeps a store of its own (OpenCode's is SQLite); several starting at once trip over its lock, "database is locked"
requirements.preconditions: configuration.executable is non-nil, so the guard at :109 has passed.
requirements.action: start() awaits the shared launch gate before spawning the child process.
requirements.expected_result: Spacing is the literal 1.5 seconds. A lone start never waits, because `slot = max(now, nextSlot)` equals now when nextSlot is in the past. A batch of N starts is released one every 1.5 s. The gate is a single static instance shared across every ACPSession of every provider and every thread, so a Cursor start and an OpenCode start issued together are still spaced 1.5 s apart.
side_effects: Delays process spawn by up to (N-1) * 1.5 s for a batch of N.
requirements.persistence: In-memory only: nextSlot lives for the life of the app process.
failure_cases: `try? await Task.sleep` swallows the sleep's error; the wait then returns early and the start proceeds.
requirements.cancellation: The sleep's thrown error is discarded by `try?`, so cancelling the awaiting task does not abort the start at this point.
requirements.windows_path: A single module-level async mutex holding nextSlot, awaited in the Electron main process before child_process.spawn. It must be one instance for the whole app, not per session, per window or per provider.
requirements.verification_method: unit (fake clock: the Nth start releases at (N-1)*1500 ms, a single start at 0 ms)

requirements.preconditions: The first openSession threw an RPCError whose message contains "auth" case-insensitively, and authMethods is non-empty.
requirements.action: ACPSession authenticates and retries the session open.
requirements.expected_result: It sends method "authenticate" with the single parameter methodId set to authMethods[0], the FIRST advertised method, with no user choice and no preference ordering. The retried openSession's failure propagates; there is no third attempt.
A provider whose unrelated error text happens to contain the letters "auth" (for example "author") triggers a spurious authenticate.
requirements.cancellation: Cancellation of the awaiting task surfaces as CancellationError from the pending request.
requirements.windows_path: Same. Use a case-insensitive indexOf on the message string; do not switch to a code check.

requirements.title: Terminating closes stdin first, then asks the process to stop, then kills it three seconds later
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:114-123 - `let handle = stdin.fileHandleForWriting; writeQueue.async { try? handle.close() }; guard process.isRunning else { return }; process.terminate(); let process = process; DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) { if process.isRunning { kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL) } }`
requirements.preconditions: stop() was called, or the connection was closed.
requirements.expected_result: Stdin is closed on the write queue, so it is ordered after any frames already queued. A process that is not running returns at that point, with no signal. Otherwise SIGTERM is sent and, exactly 3 seconds later and only if the process is still running, SIGKILL is sent to THAT PROCESS ONLY - the pid, not the process group, so grandchildren are not killed.
side_effects: The child is terminated. Any grandchildren it spawned, such as an mcp-remote npx process, are left running.
failure_cases: A child that ignores SIGTERM runs for a further 3 seconds.
requirements.windows_path: Named platform boundary. Windows has no SIGTERM with delivery semantics: per port_impacts #24, TerminateProcess is the practical equivalent and behaves like SIGKILL, so the graceful window collapses. The specification for Windows is: close stdin first, then request termination, then after the same 3 seconds force-kill if still running - preserving the ordering and the 3-second timing even though the first step is already forceful. Do NOT introduce a Job Object group kill here: the source kills the pid only, and killing the group would change observable behavior for mcp-remote grandchildren. PA-0007's Job Object candidate applies to Shell.swift, which is a different code path.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test on Windows (assert stdin closes first, the child dies, and a grandchild survives, matching macOS)

requirements.title: Stdout closing finishes the message stream, after flushing any buffered remainder

side_effects: Ends the message stream; leads to JSONRPCConnection.didClose.
requirements.windows_path: Same ordering: flush the remainder, then end the stream.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture (final frame with no trailing newline)

requirements.title: Process exit waits one second before forcing the output stream closed, because a grandchild can hold stdout open
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:164-179 - `didExit` resumes every exit waiter, then `DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1) { handle.readabilityHandler = nil; self?.finishOutput() }`; comment at :173: a grandchild can inherit stdout and keep it open after the provider exits
requirements.preconditions: The child process exited.
requirements.expected_result: Exit waiters are resumed immediately with the exit status. One second later the stdout readability handler is removed and finishOutput is forced, so a grandchild holding the pipe open cannot keep the session alive indefinitely. The delay is the literal 1 second, and it means a crashed agent's exit is reported to the chat about a second after the process died. finishOutput is idempotent in effect because continuation.finish() on an already-finished stream is a no-op.
side_effects: Delays the .exited event by about one second after a crash.
requirements.windows_path: Same 1-second forced close. It matters more on Windows, where an mcp-remote npx grandchild inheriting the handle is common and there is no process-group cleanup (see PR-PROVACP-157).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test (agent exits while a grandchild holds stdout; assert the exited event within about a second)
